## Why
These tier-2 bugs are real and they do not share a file with a tier-1 ticket, so they did not ride along. They are 1.0 work only if the tier-1 bugs are already in review and the run is ahead. The release does not wait on this ticket. Backlog: the tier-2 rows named below.

## Evidence
Each row is from `upstream-triage/c11-1.0/05-bug-reconciled.md` tier 2, with the mechanism in `05-bug-sweep-data/LEDGER.md` and the corrections in `audit-fable.md` and `audit-astra.md`. origin/main is `0ff8887e5e`. Re-find every line. Ledger lines from before C11-248 are stale. Probable rows need the trigger established or an explicit disproof. A missing reproducer is not a fix.

## Scope
One PR per group. Do not land all of these in one diff. Skip a group that the run does not reach.

Socket waits:
- B006. `v2AwaitCallback` pumps the main run loop when the caller is on main (`BrowserHandlers`, the `CFRunLoopRunInMode` path). C11-209 is the 2026-08-12 incident. Do not port upstream's fast-fail that returns nil and drops the work. Cap the timeout and refuse a WebView that never loaded.

Window and restore lifetime:
- B018. A closed main window retains its SwiftUI content through a strong window reference (`ContentView` holding the window).
- B069, probable. Closing a window drops routing refs without retiring the manager, so a late callback can still create a PTY.
- B046. Session history already keeps 10 copies (#467). What is left is holding back a poorer autosave and a way to restore from that history.
- B075, probable. Restore swaps in a new workspace graph without tearing down the old one. Do this after the Ghostty mailbox ticket so teardown can abort. `PortScanner`'s callback is already on main.
- B193. Resigning active snapshots every session on main (`AppDelegate` `applicationWillResignActive`).
- B050. Quit waits synchronously for telemetry that can wait for main (`PostHogAnalytics` flush). Skip the wait. Telemetry is best-effort on quit.
- B247, probable. Resume does not check that a live process already owns the session writer.
- B248, probable. Resume starts in the terminal's drifted directory instead of the session directory.

Focus:
- B032. The synchronous focus post is still in `Workspace`. Fable: the re-entering observer is gone on this SHA (`ContentView` no longer calls `focusTab` from it). Defer and coalesce the post. Do not rebuild focus. There is no 426-second cycle left to fix.
- B093. AppKit and Ghostty focus can disagree, so typed input sits in a terminal that does not have Ghostty focus. Reassert when this view is first responder.
- B114. `vendor/bonsplit` `SplitViewController` sets `focusedPaneId` to the sibling on every close, and `Workspace` applies it. Closing an unfocused pane steals focus. Push the bonsplit commit to its remote `main` before the parent pointer. Do not commit a detached submodule.

Portal:
- B049. Terminal portal `bind` runs `layoutSubtreeIfNeeded` inside a SwiftUI layout turn (`TerminalWindowPortal.swift`). Defer it. Do not add a display link.
- B160. Pane ownership lookup reads every tab model and subscribes portal views to title changes. Identity lookup should not subscribe to titles. The spinner filter is a different ticket. Do not depend on it.

Browser automation, not C11-287:
- B078. `browser cookies clear --url` ignores the filter and clears the shared profile (`BrowserQueryHandlers`). Honor the url or path, or require an explicit scope.
- B080. `browser state load` writes storage into the document that is still committed, then reports loaded. Wait for the navigation to commit, and keep the origin.
- Do not edit `replaceWebViewPreservingState`. C11-287 owns that function (B074, B014) and its ride-alongs B113, B120, and B162.

Theme:
- B083. `NSColor.darken` calls `getHue` without converting to sRGB, so a catalog or grayscale divider color raises (`GhosttyConfig.swift` near 644). Convert first.

Routing and input leftovers:
- B137. `GHOSTTY_ACTION_PWD` writes the directory through the key window's manager (`GhosttyTerminalView`, the case under set-title). Use the tab's own workspace, the way the notification path below it already does.
- B148. Keys that arrive before the Ghostty runtime exists are passed to `super`, so AppKit beeps or inserts them into the wrong view (`keyDown` near 5602). Consume them.

Shell wrapper:
- B064. Two copies of `Resources/bin/claude` on `PATH` can exec each other (`:49` skips only its own directory). Add a reentry guard. Check the Codex wrapper for the same finder shape and fix it if the loop is the same. Wrappers stay in the bundle. No writes to `~/.claude` or `~/.codex`.

Out:
- Every tier-1 bug. Those have their own tickets.
- Tier-2 rows that already ride a tier-1 ticket: B001, B004, B014, B015, B020, B021, B025, B029, B033, B034, B036, B037, B042, B043, B045, B060, B066, B067, B068, B089, B113, B120, B162, B166, B175, B180, B188, B189, B257, B266, B355. Do not take them.
- Tier 3, all parked: B008, B017, B026, B038, B039, B040, B041, B048, B051, B052, B053, B054, B055, B057, B063, B073, B081, B098, B112, B115, B118, B119, B121, B139, B143, B153, B171, B184, B197, B203, B295, B305, B309, B324. B051, B073, and B081 are already fixed on this SHA. Do not reopen them.
- Journal notification restore (B044). Commented on C11-231.

## Approach
Leave this ticket in the backlog until the P0 tickets in ws:bugs are in review. Then take the group with the worst operator moment that the run still has time for. Browser automation (B078, B080) is the one that breaks the `c11-browser` skill. Resume cwd and the double-writer (B247, B248) are next if agents are resuming into the wrong directory. The rest are S repairs.

Each PR names the ledger ids it closes and the ones it disproved. Update this ticket's comment with that list. Do not widen a group into a subsystem rewrite.

## Acceptance criteria
1. The release can ship with this ticket still open. Nothing in ws:bugs P0 or P1 depends on it.
2. For each group that is attempted: the operator-visible failure in that group's bullet no longer happens on a tagged build, or the PR records a disproof. Examples that count: a url-scoped cookie clear leaves other cookies, a state load lands on the new origin, closing a background pane leaves focus where it was, quit does not wait on telemetry.
3. Groups that are not attempted stay listed here, not silently dropped.

## Validation
The check matches the group: a logic test where the decision is pure, `tests_v2` for socket and browser commands, computer use where focus or a window is the bug. Builds on Atlas after C11-216. No soak unless a group touches a typing path (B032, B049, B160), in which case a short before/after sample is enough and the C11-270 soak is the real gate. No source-grep test. No Hyperion build.

## Dependencies
Ordering note, not a link: start after the Ghostty patch set and the app-half ticket are in review, because B075's teardown and B049's portal code sit next to that work. Cross-workstream: F1 is C11-216, F2 is C11-270. C11-287 owns the browser host crash. The lead links across workstreams.

## Risks
A sweep PR that collides with a tier-1 owner in `GhosttyTerminalView`, `SurfaceHandlers`, `ContentView`, or `BrowserTab`. Read those tickets' ride-alongs before editing. Bonsplit and Ghostty submodule pointers follow the push-first rule. Doctrine: no tenant config writes. New UI strings use `String(localized:)` and the translation ticket. Public repo: name the bug and the outcome. No trigger recipes, no crash payloads.

Size: M. Tier: P2. Doctrine check: holding list. One group per PR. No tenant config.

## C11-311 validation

- Final branch: `c11-1.0/C11-311-cookie-state`
- Final HEAD: `36cb0a8cdccac3bd4936d917bb785c90a5d7757b`
- Base: `origin/main` `ef36ab825825387c2a9c3eb941261b831ec1c010`
- C11-314 deletion commit `9f2173320a` is an ancestor of HEAD.
- Working tree: clean.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: passed.

### Atlas targeted gate

Command:

```text
./scripts/remote-build.sh --tag c11-311-cookie-state --mode test -- -only-testing:c11LogicTests -skip-testing:c11LogicTests/SocketControlPasswordStoreTests -resultBundlePath c11-311-cookie-state-final-2.xcresult
```

Result: invocation `a2458b71678c405a885088ea2c0689dc`; compile `ok`; tests `ok`. The only explicit skip was `SocketControlPasswordStoreTests`, whose SSH Keychain path is not runnable in the guest. C11-314's deleted `WorkspaceRemoteConnectionTests` is not skipped because it no longer exists.

### Atlas tagged artifact

Command:

```text
./scripts/remote-build.sh --tag c11-311-cookie-state --mode debug
```

Result: invocation `5728ccbf3fd84ee6a50f905ce4391fb5`; compile `ok`; artifact retrieved as:

`/Users/atin/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/c11-c11-311-cookie-state/Build/Products/Debug/c11 DEV c11-311-cookie-state.app`

### Validator scenario

1. Launch that tagged app in a fresh isolated Atlas Tart guest with `C11_QA_LAUNCH=fresh`.
2. Run `scripts/sandbox-tests-v2.sh <run-id> tests_v2/test_browser_api_extended_families.py`.
3. Verify an unscoped `browser.cookies.clear` is rejected without deleting cookies; a URL-scoped clear removes only the matching loopback host cookie; explicit `all:true` retains profile-wide clear behavior.
4. Verify `browser.state.load` sets cookies before navigation, waits for the delayed target origin to commit, then restores target local/session storage; storage from the prior origin is absent.
5. Verify a redirect to the wrong origin returns a bounded navigation failure and does not write the target storage.
6. Delete the guest immediately after the run with `scripts/sandbox-down.sh <run-id>`.

The focused guest run was attempted twice but could not acquire a lease: both Atlas Tart slots were actively held by `c11-sb-val-4-core` and another active validation/UI guest; `sandbox-up.sh` refused the third clone and cleaned its staged app. No runtime pass is claimed here. The Atlas logic gate and tagged build above are the completed pre-handoff checks; the scenario is ready for the batch Validator.

### Scope

This slice covers B078/B080 only. Other C11-311 groups remain unattempted on the ticket. No installed skill copy was synced, and no PR was opened before handoff.

# C11-311 review, cycle 1

Verdict: **FAIL**

PR #538, head `36cb0a8cdccac3bd4936d917bb785c90a5d7757b`, merge-base `ef36ab825825387c2a9c3eb941261b831ec1c010`. Fetched main and the linked branch, independently confirmed the open PR's head, and reviewed all eight changed files plus their routing, cookie-construction, JavaScript and navigation seams. The detached checkout was clean; `git diff --check` passed. No builds, tests or app launches were performed by this reviewer.

## Blocking

1. **B078: URL-scoped clear still deletes cookies outside the URL's request scope.** `Sources/SocketHandlers/BrowserQueryHandlers.swift:110-114` strips the leading dot before unconditionally allowing a host suffix match. A host-only cookie with domain `example.com` and path `/account` is therefore deleted by a clear for `https://app.example.com/account/settings`, even though that cookie does not apply to the subdomain. This is the same destructive scope failure the B078 slice must prevent. Apple's [HTTPCookie.domain documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/httpcookie/domain) specifies exact-host matching for domains without the leading dot. The new behavioral test actually locks in the incorrect result at `c11Tests/BrowserAwaitPolicyTests.swift:97`, also at lines 103 and 109. Smallest fix: retain the host-only/domain-cookie distinction for URL matching; allow the suffix branch only for domain cookies. Correct the expectations and cover host-only parent, exact host, and dotted parent-domain cookies. No matcher framework is needed.

2. **The numbered Validator scenario's two-origin cookie fixture creates both cookies on one host and stops before the B080 checks.** `tests_v2/test_browser_api_extended_families.py:302-315` supplies only `url: other_origin_url` for `scoped_other` while the tab remains on `127.0.0.1`. The unchanged setter captures the current page as `fallbackURL` (`Sources/SocketHandlers/BrowserQueryHandlers.swift:1123-1124`); the constructor then explicitly assigns that fallback host to `.domain` whenever the row lacks a domain (lines 1067-1070), despite having assigned the supplied URL to `.originURL`. Foundation infers the domain from originURL only when the domain attribute is absent, per [Apple's domain-property documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/httpcookiepropertykey/domain). Both fixture cookies consequently belong to `127.0.0.1`; the subsequent URL clear deletes both and the line-315 assertion fails. This is a static fixture defect, not a claim that the deferred run was executed. Smallest fix: seed the other cookie with an explicit `localhost` domain (or through a response from that host), and assert both stored domains before the clear. Keep the unrelated setter repair out of this slice unless deliberately admitted. The corrected test must reach the delayed-load and wrong-origin redirect assertions.

## Non-blocking

1. `Sources/Tabs/BrowserTab.swift:2880-2898` completes the state-load wait from `didFinish`, whereas the new comment at line 4226 and skill reference describe navigation commit. Apple distinguishes [main-frame commit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/webkit/wknavigationdelegate/webview(_:didcommit:)) from [navigation completion](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/webkit/wknavigationdelegate/webview(_:didfinish:)). Waiting for finish can make a committed target with slow resources consume the navigation timeout. Clarify the documented wait, or use the existing delegate's commit event if commit is the intended readiness point. This is not an additional blocking demand for a new navigation mechanism.

Scope remains B078/B080. The worker-dispatch changes support the admitted cookie/state waits and are explicitly covered by the plan's takeover correction. No typing hot path, journal/attention seam, tenant-config write, `replaceWebViewPreservingState` edit, or unrelated refactor was found. The source adds protocol diagnostics, with no new graphical UI copy. The validation comment honestly leaves other groups unattempted; B075 remains deferred. The ticket must remain a holding ticket for those slices.

## Runtime proof still required

The owner reports an Atlas logic-test pass and tagged build in validation event `ev_01M3YPS1SWTKM7Q1NV9E211K13`; this review did not independently execute those gates. The owner explicitly reports no socket/runtime pass. At PR inspection, build and compatibility CI were still in progress.

Deferring this low-risk slice's runtime proof to the merged-main Validator batch is allowed. That deferral is not a reason for FAIL; the two findings above are.

After repair, retain the owner's numbered Atlas guest scenario and verify:

1. Matcher regressions distinguish host-only and domain cookies; URL/path/secure filtering and ambiguous or unscoped clear rejection remain correct.
2. The real cookie fixture proves distinct hosts before clearing, preserves the other host, and verifies explicit `all: true` separately. Assert that rejected unscoped clearing leaves both cookies intact.
3. The socket test reaches both B080 cases: delayed target navigation restores local/session storage on the target, and a wrong-origin redirect fails without applying storage. Verify the target request receives the restored cookie and revisit the old origin to confirm its storage was not changed.
4. Required CI passes at the repaired head; run the corrected socket scenario in the isolated Atlas tagged-app batch. Do not describe static review or the recorded build as runtime proof.

C11-311 review repair, round 1 (Astra event `ev_01M3YQ27A5JS34AK3JXDCWF6YB`): B078 URL scoping now allows suffix matching only for domain cookies whose stored domain begins with a dot; host-only cookies match only an exact host. The matcher tests cover a host-only parent, exact host-only host, and dotted parent-domain cookie. The B078/B080 socket fixture assigns the second cookie to explicit `localhost`, verifies the stored domains differ before clearing, verifies an unscoped clear preserves both, URL-scoped clear removes only the target, and explicit `all: true` removes the other cookie. B080 also verifies the restored cookie is sent on the target request, local/session storage lands only after the target navigation finishes, the old origin's storage is unchanged on revisit, and a wrong-origin redirect fails without storage mutation. The non-blocking API wording now says navigation finish, matching the existing `didFinish` implementation.

Pushed review head `d28f8689d33d5b640c9ec1693b5b1c4230330ebf`; draft PR #538: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/538. Only B078/B080 are in this PR; all other C11-311 groups remain unattempted.

Atlas logic validation: invocation `c51c0b539e71426b8cc0bf56f45f8c1e`, tag `c11-311`, source head `09f7112b2ad9b693213303c3a7f5e4eec5b011bb`; `c11LogicTests` selected, `SocketControlPasswordStoreTests` skipped over SSH/Keychain. Result: 2,379 tests executed, 3 skipped, 0 failures. `BrowserAwaitPolicyTests.testCookieClearFilterRequiresAnUnambiguousScope` and `.testCookieClearURLFilterMatchesCookieScope` passed. `WorkspaceRemoteConnectionTests` ran (2 tests, 0 failures); no skip was applied to that suite. The only changes after this test head are documentation merges.

Atlas tagged Debug build: invocation `85ad609f675c444ea095b4018f44fc16`, tag `c11-311`, exact repaired head `d28f8689d33d5b640c9ec1693b5b1c4230330ebf`; compile passed and the app was retrieved at the canonical tag path.

Runtime status: the first guest run stopped in an unrelated browser-dialog fixture at `browser.addscript`, before the C11-311 checks. The fixture now schedules dialogs one second after `addscript` returns. A retry was refused because both shared Tart guests were active; the failed clone was automatically removed. No socket/runtime pass is claimed here.

Command correction note: an initial unfiltered `c11-unit` invocation reached host tests and failed at `AppDelegateShortcutRoutingTests.testCmdWClosesAuxiliaryWindowInsteadOfMainTerminalPanel`; I stopped that unrelated host-suite run and reran the intended logic-only selection successfully.

Validator scenario (isolated guest, tagged app `c11-311`):
1. Run `scripts/sandbox-tests-v2.sh <run-id> tests_v2/test_browser_api_extended_families.py` against the tagged app.
2. Confirm the fixture stores one cookie for `127.0.0.1` and one for `localhost`; rejected unscoped clear preserves both, URL clear deletes only the selected host's cookie, and `all: true` deletes the remaining cookie.
3. Confirm `browser.state.load` returns only after navigation to the target origin finishes; the target request contains the restored cookie; target local/session storage is present, old-origin storage is unchanged on revisit, and a wrong-origin redirect returns `navigation_failed` without applying storage.

# C11-311 delta review, round 2

Verdict: **FAIL**

PR #538 head: `d28f8689d33d5b640c9ec1693b5b1c4230330ebf`.

Scope: the four repair commits `5cccbe86b6`, `2d0c9bc68e`, `33bd35076b`, and `3662ebc92b`, reviewed as `git diff c45b4e3d82 3662ebc92b`, plus verification of the main merges. No fresh whole-PR audit.

The actual round-1 review event `ev_01M3YQ27A5JS34AK3JXDCWF6YB` covered `36cb0a8cdccac3bd4936d917bb785c90a5d7757b`. Supplied base `c45b4e3d82` is its immediate main merge. That merge and `09f7112b2a` and `d28f8689d3` all have empty `git show --remerge-diff` output and second parents on fetched main. The final two merges change only four documentation files; none of the five repair-delta files differs between `3662ebc92b` and the reviewed head. PR head verified live; detached checkout clean; diff whitespace check passed.

## Blocking

1. **The dialog-sequencing repair still prevents the fresh-guest Validator scenario from reaching B078/B080.** `tests_v2/test_browser_api_extended_families.py:268-278` schedules `window.triggerDialogs()` for 1000 ms, sleeps 1100 ms, and only then makes its first `browser.dialog.accept` call. Before the timer fires, neither the page nor this fixture has installed the dialog overrides: `browser.console.list` installs only console/error hooks (`Sources/SocketHandlers/BrowserQueryHandlers.swift:833-848,1542-1544`), and the document-start script is also only that telemetry bootstrap (`Sources/Tabs/BrowserTab.swift:2783-2790`). The separate dialog bootstrap is installed by `v2BrowserDialogRespond` at lines 851-855, after the timer has already called native `confirm`.

   The socket responder consumes `window.__cmuxDialogQueue`; it does not answer the native NSAlert (`BrowserQueryHandlers.swift:860-882`, `BrowserTab.swift:7194-7249`). On a visible guest window the first confirm can hold the page while the responder tries to evaluate JavaScript; if native dialogs are instead safely dismissed, their events were never queued and the first accept returns `not_found`. Delaying the trigger lets `addscript` return but does not establish the necessary interception. This is the reported pre-cookie fixture incident in owner validation `ev_01M3YTM8H5B2FRFHNY9A0AY7Q3`, not a new unrelated product requirement.

   **Smallest fix:** prime the existing dialog handler before triggering the fixture, for example call `browser.dialog.dismiss` on the initially empty queue and require its expected `not_found`, which installs the overrides. Then trigger and consume the three queued dialogs. Avoid relying on a sleep to establish hook installation. Verify that this scenario reaches the cookie and state assertions in the isolated Atlas guest.

## Resolved round-1 findings

- **Host-only cookie scope:** fixed. `BrowserCookieClearFilter` now permits suffix matching only when the stored domain begins with a dot. Exact-host and dotted-domain behavior remain covered.
- **Two-origin cookie construction:** fixed. The second cookie explicitly sets `domain: localhost`, and the fixture asserts both stored domains before deletion. Rejected unscoped clear preservation, scoped deletion, and explicit `all: true` now have separate assertions. The remaining blocker is reaching these assertions through the repaired dialog prefix.
- **Non-blocking navigation wording:** resolved. Source and skill now describe navigation finish, matching the existing `didFinish` behavior. The fixture also checks the target request's restored cookie and revisits the old origin to check that its storage was preserved.

## Non-blocking

None added. The readiness retry is restricted to `not_ready` and bounded to 30 seconds. No product changes beyond the narrow cookie-domain guard were added by the repair delta.

## Runtime proof still required

**Independent mutation proof completed on Atlas.** A scratch Swift package compiled the exact `BrowserCookieClearFilter` source and the two checked-in cookie test methods plus their cookie helper from the reviewed head. This uses real Foundation cookies and XCTest, without the app or WebKit. The package wrapper supplies only test discovery. No checkout source was edited.

Commands: `swift test --package-path control --jobs 1` and the same command with `mutant`. The mutant changes only:

```swift
return host == cookie || (isDomainCookie && host.hasSuffix(".\(cookie)"))
```

back to:

```swift
return host == cookie || host.hasSuffix(".\(cookie)")
```

Results: repaired control exit 0, two tests passed; mutant exit 1, `testCookieClearURLFilterMatchesCookieScope` failed three `XCTAssertFalse` assertions for host-only parent cookies. The unambiguous-scope test still passed. This proves the repaired guard is protected by a test that goes red when the original behavior returns; it does not claim a full app test run.

**Dialog-order probe completed on Atlas.** Executed the exact checked-in telemetry bootstrap, fixture trigger/timer, and dialog bootstrap in a Node VM with native-dialog sentinels. With the checked-in order, all three native sentinels fired and the queue was empty. Installing the existing dialog bootstrap before the trigger produced zero native calls and queued `confirm`, `prompt`, `alert`. This is an executable JavaScript ordering probe, not a WKWebView or packaged-app runtime pass.

Evidence is retained locally under `/tmp/c11-311-r2-mutation-d28f868/`: `manifest.json`, `merge-check.json`, both scratch packages, `control.log`, `mutant.log`, `results.txt`, and the dialog-order scripts/log. The essential outcomes are embedded above so this review does not depend on the scratch directory surviving.

Owner event `ev_01M3YTM8H5B2FRFHNY9A0AY7Q3` reports 2,379 Atlas logic tests with zero failures at `09f7112b2a` and a tagged build at the exact review head, but explicitly claims no socket/runtime pass. The intervening merge is documentation-only. At live inspection required CI was still running.

The low-risk batch-runtime deferral remains allowed and is not itself a reason for FAIL. After correcting the fixture prefix, required CI must pass and the numbered isolated-guest scenario must reach both cookie and state-load assertions in the Validator batch. No Hyperion tests, app launch, commit, push, merge, or GitHub comment was performed.

Round 3 owner validation for C11-311 at `8d78d58000d37f9721c99caf0caa09a5e415d767`.

- Fixed only `tests_v2/test_browser_api_extended_families.py`: call `browser.dialog.dismiss` while the queue is empty and require `not_found` to install the dialog overrides, then synchronously trigger and consume the three queued dialogs. There is no sleep for hook installation.
- `python3 -m py_compile tests_v2/test_browser_api_extended_families.py` passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- Atlas isolated guest, tag `c11-311`, run `c11-311-r3`: `scripts/sandbox-tests-v2.sh c11-311-r3 tests_v2/test_browser_api_extended_families.py` passed (`passed=1 failed=0`). The complete scenario returned PASS, so it continued beyond dialog handling through the B078 cookie-scope assertions and the B080 delayed state-load/storage/request-cookie assertions.
- The guest used the existing tagged Debug app (`com.stage11.c11.debug.c11.311`), since this repair changes only the Python fixture. The test log was retrieved, then `scripts/sandbox-down.sh c11-311-r3` deleted `c11-sb-c11-311-r3`.

No other C11-311 bug-sweep groups are claimed as attempted.

# C11-311 delta review, round 3

Verdict: **PASS**

PR #538, exact head `8d78d58000d37f9721c99caf0caa09a5e415d767`, review base `d28f8689d33d5b640c9ec1693b5b1c4230330ebf`. Live PR head and clean detached checkout verified; `git diff --check` passed. Reviewed only the one remaining dialog-fixture blocker from event `ev_01M3YV15TYAB0NWX2M520Y8QDV`.

## Blocking

None. The only changed file is `tests_v2/test_browser_api_extended_families.py`. At lines 269-273, it calls `browser.dialog.dismiss` on the empty queue and requires `not_found` before synchronously calling `window.triggerDialogs()` at lines 274-277. The unchanged responder installs the dialog overrides before testing whether its queue is empty (`Sources/SocketHandlers/BrowserQueryHandlers.swift:851-889`). Thus the trigger reaches the installed queueing overrides instead of native confirm. The timer and installation sleep have both been removed. The three response assertions and empty-queue check remain intact.

## Non-blocking

None in this delta. Prior resolved findings were not reopened.

## Runtime proof still required

None for this remaining blocker. Independently read the retained Atlas evidence for isolated guest run `c11-311-r3`, corroborating owner validation `ev_01M3YVHYVT3H1Q72R6BZTW3FP7`:

- Host output `.c11-sandbox/out/c11-311-r3/tests-v2.log` contains `PASS: extended browser parity families are green`.
- The staged fixture at `.c11-sandbox/out/c11-311-r3/suite-src/tests_v2/test_browser_api_extended_families.py` and the exact reviewed-head file both have SHA-256 `5857b55f5f313c3e4576b64a19433703ecd3cef926da42dba68796348b4a0508`.
- Inspected `scripts/sandbox-tests-v2.sh`: it copies that staged suite into the guest, relaunches the guest app, and executes the selected Python file against the guest socket. The test's final PASS line is reached only after the dialog sequence, cookie domain/preservation/scoped-clear/all-clear checks, and state-load target storage/request-cookie/old-origin preservation/wrong-origin rejection checks. Those assertions are unconditional and raise on failure.
- The owner records `passed=1 failed=0` with tagged app `c11-311`. Reusing the prior tagged app is appropriate because this delta changes only the Python fixture. The retained guest and run-metadata paths are absent after the owner's cleanup.

This is independent inspection of the owner's retained runtime evidence, not a claim that the reviewer launched or reran the guest. The retrieved log is also retained locally as `/tmp/review-C11-311-r3-atlas-tests-v2.log`. The prior Atlas cookie mutation proof remains recorded in round 2.

PASS closes the one remaining review blocker at this head. It does not claim CI completion, merge, release, or completion of the ticket's deferred sweep groups. No source edits, builds, tests, app launches, commits, pushes, merges, or GitHub comments were performed in this review.

# C11-311 slice 2 review, cycle 1

Verdict: **FAIL**

PR #546, head `0b5f04dbeaf5a39de08c2c35d7308a056d266b70`, merge-base `bc915d0509187b67ba97ef66dce28609acf373eb`. Fetched main and the branch; verified the live PR head and clean detached checkout. Reviewed the complete two-file diff and the window assignment, notification, controller, close-routing and termination seams. `git diff --check` passed. No source edits, builds, tests or app launches were performed by this reviewer.

## Blocking

1. **The regression and numbered Validator scenario do not test B018's retained window/content failure.** `c11Tests/WindowAndDragTests.swift:1189-1195` asserts that a closed window no longer changes a titlebar accessory, drops its strong local reference, then ends without any lifetime assertion. A closed window and its hosting content can remain retained indefinitely and this test still passes. The numbered scenario in validation event `ev_01M3YXQ20XEPKY8X1W0Q2RCY60` repeats exactly that observation-only oracle. This does not fulfill the plan's explicit requirement at `.lattice/plans/task_01M3X6K35PP4W75VV5XV9VGYXS.md:209`: “Window-retain proof uses a weak reference that actually deallocates after close.” The ticket's B018 row and `upstream-triage/c11-1.0/05-bug-sweep-data/LEDGER.md:85` concern retained SwiftUI content, not synthetic fullscreen notifications.

   Smallest correction: retain the useful observation test, and supply a bounded lifetime fixture/scenario through the real window/content close path that releases its own strong references and asserts weak window/hosting-content release. Establish that the harness's plain-window control releases too; the owner's failed plain-window control explains why its first oracle was unusable, but is not a disproof of B018. Preserve red/green evidence for the lifetime oracle with only the production fix removed/restored. Include the brief's close button, last-tab Cmd-W, programmatic close and quit paths in the Validator scenario, recording the quit lifecycle separately where process exit is the applicable outcome. No teardown framework or unrelated lifetime repair is requested. Alternatively record a supported disproof and stop claiming B018 fixed.

   This is an inadequate acceptance scenario, which the batch-validation contract calls a finding. FAIL is not based merely on deferring execution to the merged-main batch, and is not a claim that the six-line fix has been demonstrated to leak.

## Non-blocking

None.

The source mechanism remains present on fetched main `43c1d51901c7c9048d9f5c5a97319c26bf445f6a`: strong `@State observedWindow`, assigned by the WindowAccessor, with no close reset. The patch resets only the identical observed window. The accessor's coordinator is weak and deduplicates the same window. The normal close button and programmatic routes converge on window close; Apple's [NSWindow.close documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nswindow/close()) confirms that close posts willCloseNotification. This is a reasonable narrow repair. The termination methods contain no explicit observed-window clearing, so the synthetic close test must not be described as quit-path proof.

The diff adds no typing-path work in TabItemView, hitTest or forceRefresh, no teardown, no tenant-config writes, no new product strings and no socket/threading changes. B078/B080 and the remaining sweep groups are outside this review. B018 is already an upstream ledger item; no additional upstream submission is needed to establish this review's scope.

## Runtime proof still required

Independently inspected the owner's retained Atlas `result.json` and `build.log` files:

- `071a69d43ac147428731c4da5626409d`: base head plus test overlay, compile succeeded, one host test failed with the expected post-close accessory assertions (XCTAssertFalse and alpha 0 versus 1). This establishes stale observation before the fix. The earlier test has a different class name and file hash, so it is not an independently reproduced mutation of the final exact test.
- `cba0180f1b664659a2e2d62dd8206379`: same base plus production/test overlays, compile succeeded, one host test passed. Both overlay SHA256 values match the two files at the reviewed head, and the commit changes only those files. This is valid recorded proof for the shipped observation test. It is not lifetime proof.

The reviewer did not break or rerun the code, respecting the read-only/no-Hyperion-tests contract. Atlas must supply the repaired lifetime oracle and its mutation result. The low-risk tagged-app close-path scenario may run in the authorized Validator batch once its oracle is adequate. Required landing gates remain the Captain's responsibility; observed fast PR checks were successful with Drawbridge skipped. No merge, release or completion of C11-311 is claimed.
